purpose: Quadratic/cubic device quotient compilation, evaluation, hiding commitment and scalar next-point support
result: 96 quotient arithmetic/commitment comparisons, 12 owned adapter comparisons and 48 hiding commitments match CPU references; PCS/wallet/recursive regressions pass

owned_pcs.input_openings: All produced from the GPU commitments and their retained prefixes; no CPU input proofs are attached.
owned_pcs.strict_policy: gpu_required in wide/narrow release and wide debug for operation scope
owned_pcs.arithmetic_conformance: Both pinned extensions, mixed matrix widths, 1–32 points including duplicates, multiple cosets, tiles and Goldilocks boundary values; CPU Horner evaluation and independent reduction formulas.
owned_pcs.scope: Public base-evaluation and opening-point fixtures are supplied outside the operation. This is an owned two-adic PCS opening component, not a complete hiding PCS or legacy STARK adapter.

general_fri.protocol: Pinned quadratic u^2=7 and existing cubic basis; no protocol parameters or proof encodings changed.
general_fri.pow_comparison: The CPU reference checks and replays each GPU PoW witness. Upstream parallel grinding may select a different valid nonce; byte equality is conditioned on the same independently checked witnesses.
general_fri.scope: GPU FRI operation from uploaded public reduced-input fixtures. CPU-generated input matrix openings are attached outside that operation. This does not establish a complete legacy quadratic STARK/PCS GPU path.

candidate_entrypoints.selection: The complete explicitly initialized owned OpenCL selection routes compatible and GPU-required requests to the owned prover. Other selections retain existing policy admission; strict requests cannot fall back to CPU.
candidate_entrypoints.lifecycle: GPU selection remains configured after engine shutdown. A resident-engine check rejects later requests before the infallible configuration constructor, for both GPU-required and compatible policy, without reinitialization or CPU fallback.
candidate_entrypoints.authorization: The host independently authorizes nonzero in-range mint and issuance count. The request checks the witness amount before private work and rechecks the GPU-produced public mint before proving. No authority is granted by the proof API.
admission_controls: issuance attempted through spend or HTLC route
retired backend under strict or compatible policy
candidate_entrypoints.debug_cpu_audit: Explicit constraint audit remains; trace reads are 622592 bytes for join-split/issuance and 1179648 bytes for HTLC per proof

pilot_notes: Pilot 05 passes all five targeted checks: quadratic hiding commitments in full/compact storage, cubic hiding commitments, three quadratic PCS proofs and seven candidate wallet proofs.
Initial library/test builds exposed existing API-name and generic test-bound mismatches; corrected builds and logs are retained.

Pilots 01/02 pass both scalar suites and both quotient arithmetic suites. Hiding fixtures initially used a resident CPU oracle, omitted explicit owned consumers, and expected host-retained data. They now use upstream CPU HidingFriPcs, explicit GPU openings/randomness and the owned-query comparator with CPU verification. Production guards remain intact.
validator_notes: All test counts are reparsed from hashed logs. Owned PCS reports must cover exactly nine stages with positive GPU calls/time, zero observation errors and strict completion.
The existing FRI suite still requires six complete reports and six CPU verifications per field/profile. CPU reference PoW replay validates each GPU witness independently before matching proof bytes.
limitations: NVIDIA laptop OpenCL correctness qualification only; no transaction throughput or AMD/Metal qualification.
Public component fixtures do not constitute complete legacy quadratic STARK proofs. Generic resident/hiding PCS configuration, witness integration and legacy Rust/C ABI routing remain unfinished.
Candidate protocol parameters and proof encodings are unchanged. Debug whole-STARK proofs retain their explicit CPU constraint audits.

Private wallet worker admission, owned multi-AIR commitments, full-size recursive workloads, resource calibration and sustained throughput remain open. Apple source requires its authorized local Mac checkpoint commit.

quotient.domains: Both direct full-domain evaluation and GPU coset partition/interleave; nonzero extension alpha and zero alpha.
quotient.constraints: Mixed base/extension assertions in global order, local/next main/preprocessed/permutation rows, public inputs, challenges, terminals, constants, selectors and vanishing-polynomial division.
quotient.transfers: The 96 arithmetic/commitment cases pass quotient values to GPU commitments before value readback. The 12 extra adapter cases read final values for comparison. Scalar/domain metadata and validation status remain host-visible; hiding samples are generated and consumed on GPU.
quotient.hiding_reference: Independent upstream CPU HidingFriPcs with matching deterministic test-only streams; comparisons include retained prefixes, commitment caps and query paths.
quotient.scope: Component correctness from public input matrices. Complete legacy quadratic hiding PCS/STARK configuration and witness integration remain open.

scalar.coverage: Compact quadratic outputs, field boundaries and zero, malformed encodings rejected before work, empty challenger requests and unchanged transcript sampling.
